contract.name: PasswordInput
contract.summary: Sorleed's password field: label, masked text control, show/hide toggle, helper or error and an independent focus ring. It composes the existing input.* and button.* component tokens plus four documented primitive tokens. The Figma reference is unresolved and is not asserted.
contract.maturity: contract; framework-agnostic CSS + native HTML; React private-alpha adapter

evidence: The Figma reference is unresolved. No node ID, variant ID or property key is asserted by this contract.
components/password-input/password-input.css and password-input.html are the canonical framework-agnostic implementation.
react/password-input/index.tsx is a private-alpha adapter and is not represented as production-ready.
The stylesheet composes input.* and button.* component tokens and four primitive tokens; the primitive use is a recorded draft limitation.
No password-strength, breach-check, caps-lock or confirmation behaviour is implemented.

component: Render the full field anatomy: label, control with password input and toggle button, and a helper or error row.
Switch the native input type between password and text without changing the entered value.
Expose the toggle as a native button with an accessible name and aria-pressed state.
Apply input.* and button.* component tokens for the documented surfaces and states.
Expose native disabled, required and readOnly attributes passed by the application.
Suppress the focus ring when the field is disabled.
application: Own password policy, validation timing, error copy and announcements.
Choose the appropriate autoComplete token for the password's purpose.
Provide a visible required indication when required is set.
Decide whether visibility starts shown or hidden when using controlled visibility.
Handle form submission and move focus to the first invalid field.
Never log, persist or expose the entered password outside the form flow.
figmaOnly: No Figma evidence is recorded for this component. Design-time property mapping is not asserted.

intended: Collecting a password or passphrase in sign-in, registration and account-security forms.
Allowing the user to reveal the entered value to reduce typing errors on shared or small keyboards.

inappropriate.use: Using PasswordInput as a general text field.
inappropriate.reason: The masking and reveal affordance are specific to secrets and the component composes password-specific behaviour.
inappropriate.alternative: Use Input for non-secret single-line text.

inappropriate.use: Using PasswordInput as a search, OTP, PIN or currency field.
inappropriate.reason: Those controls need different masking, grouping, input modes and validation.
inappropriate.alternative: Use a dedicated component when its contract exists; do not fake it with type or CSS overrides.

inappropriate.use: Adding a strength meter, breach check or caps-lock warning through this component.
inappropriate.reason: No such behaviour, tokens or accessible announcement pattern exists in this contract.
inappropriate.alternative: Request a new contract and token roles before implementing those capabilities.

structure: Password input with class .sl-password-input__field and type=password or type=text
Toggle button with class .sl-password-input__toggle, aria-pressed and an accessible label
Message row with class .sl-password-input__message; error adds .sl-password-input__message--error

literals.reason: Derived from input.border-width plus a 2px visual inset; no inset token exists.
A visual inset inside the control; no token exists for this local adjustment.
A local optical adjustment to fit the toggle text inside the reserved area.
No opacity token exists. The native disabled attribute remains the semantic signal.

codeOnlyProperties.description: Visible label text and accessible name for the password input.
codeOnlyProperties.notes: Must be non-empty. When hideLabel is true the label is visually hidden, not removed.

codeOnlyProperties.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it programmatically associated.
codeOnlyProperties.notes: Do not use display:none or aria-hidden on the only label.

codeOnlyProperties.description: Supporting copy shown when there is no error.
codeOnlyProperties.notes: Replaced by errorMessage when an error is present.

codeOnlyProperties.description: Error copy shown in the message row and connected through aria-describedby.
codeOnlyProperties.notes: Sets aria-invalid=true. The application owns when validation runs.

codeOnlyProperties.description: Accessible label and visible text for the toggle while the password is hidden.
codeOnlyProperties.notes: Localise this copy in the application; do not rely on an icon alone.

codeOnlyProperties.description: Accessible label and visible text for the toggle while the password is visible.
codeOnlyProperties.notes: Localise this copy in the application; do not rely on an icon alone.
When provided, the component does not update visibility internally; onVisibleChange reports the requested next state.

codeOnlyProperties.description: Initial visibility for the uncontrolled adapter.
codeOnlyProperties.notes: Defaults to masked. Not applied while visible is controlled.

codeOnlyProperties.description: Called with the requested next visibility when the toggle is activated.
codeOnlyProperties.notes: The adapter does not change the value of the password field.

codeOnlyProperties.description: Identifier for the password input and its label association.
Layout-only escape hatch for the wrapper.
codeOnlyProperties.notes: Must not change colour, typography, radius, height, border, gaps or focus treatment.

codeOnlyProperties.description: Disables both the password input and the toggle.
codeOnlyProperties.notes: Native disabled attribute; suppresses the focus ring and removes both controls from interaction.

codeOnlyProperties.description: Sets the native required attribute on the password input.
codeOnlyProperties.notes: The application owns required validation and a visible required indication.

codeOnlyProperties.description: Native autocomplete token for the password's purpose.
codeOnlyProperties.notes: The adapter defaults to current-password. Pass new-password for registration or other appropriate tokens for the context.

codeOnlyProperties.description: Passes the native readOnly attribute to the password input.
codeOnlyProperties.notes: ReadOnly has no dedicated visual treatment in the stylesheet. Do not present it as a distinct state.

codeOnlyProperties.description: Standard attributes such as placeholder, maxLength, pattern, name, aria-* and data-* pass through.
codeOnlyProperties.notes: The adapter owns type and must not receive type from the caller.

variants.name: Default
variants.notes: White fill, input.border boundary, primary text and tertiary placeholder; the toggle uses Ghost button tokens.

variants.name: Hover
variants.notes: The field border changes to input.border-hover; the toggle shows its hover background.

variants.name: Error
variants.notes: The error border is keyed to aria-invalid=true and the message carries input.text-error.

variants.name: Disabled
variants.notes: Muted fill, matching border and muted text. The toggle is disabled, reduced in opacity and cannot be activated.

validCombinations.result: Masked or revealed value, input.border boundary and the toggle at rest.
input.border-hover boundary and the toggle hover background.
Muted fill, matching border, muted text and a disabled toggle.
The input type is password; the toggle label is showPasswordLabel and aria-pressed is false.
The input type is text; the toggle label is hidePasswordLabel and aria-pressed is true.
Default boundary plus the input focus ring.
Error boundary and message plus the input focus ring.
Disabled wins; the focus ring is suppressed and the toggle is not focusable.
The error border persists; the hover border is not applied.
Disabled wins; no error border or error-coloured message.

precedence: State precedence: Disabled > Error > Hover > Default.
Focus is an orthogonal overlay in Default, Hover and Error; Disabled suppresses it.
Disabled suppresses error and hover treatment and disables the toggle.
Visibility is independent of State: the entered value is preserved when the type changes.
conflicts: Error + Hover is not modelled. Do not add a hover border on top of the error border.
Disabled + Error is not modelled. Do not show an error border or error message on a disabled field.
Disabled + Focused is not a visible combination. The focus ring must be suppressed.
Focus is not a State value. Do not create State=Focus.
Visible is not a State value. Do not create State=Visible or a separate masked/revealed variant.
The toggle must not be a div or span; it is a native button with an accessible name.
notes: The input type changes between password and text; the value is not transformed.
The toggle uses button.* Ghost tokens because no password-input.* token family exists.
The React adapter defaults autoComplete to current-password; the application should override it for new passwords.
No Figma evidence is recorded; state names are production descriptions only.

tokens.rule: PasswordInput composes the existing input.* and button.* component tokens and four documented primitive tokens (font.size.xs, font.line-height.xs, space.12, space.4). It introduces no password-input.* token family. Primitive use is a draft limitation, not a precedent for new components.

dependencies.name: input.padding-x
dependencies.role: Field horizontal padding and toggle inset

forbidden: Do not introduce password-input.* tokens without a token-source change and a new contract version.
Do not consume additional primitive or semantic tokens beyond the four documented primitives.
Do not hardcode values when a token exists.
Do not use button.* tokens for the password field surface; they are limited to the toggle.
Do not add a success, warning, info or strength token.

design.requirement: The label must be programmatically associated with the password input.
design.verification: Inspect the for/id association and the computed accessible name.

design.requirement: The toggle must have a visible text label and an accessible name that describes the next action.
design.verification: Inspect the computed accessible name and visible text in both visibility states.

design.requirement: The toggle must expose aria-pressed matching the visibility state.
design.verification: Inspect aria-pressed before and after activation.

design.requirement: Error messages must be associated with the password input.
The input and toggle must show a visible focus indicator.
design.verification: Tab to each control and inspect the rendered focus treatment.

production.requirement: The input and toggle must be keyboard reachable and operable with native controls.
production.verification: Keyboard-only test; confirm Tab order, Enter/Space activation and no keyboard trap.

production.requirement: Toggling visibility must not change, trim or re-enter the value.
production.verification: Toggle with short and long values and compare the DOM value before and after.

production.requirement: Use the native disabled attribute on both controls and do not present an error while disabled.
production.verification: Assert disabled, absence from interaction and no aria-invalid presentation.

production.requirement: Error is communicated by a border and a text message, not colour alone.
production.verification: Render an error and inspect the message text and grayscale rendering.

production.requirement: Supply the correct autocomplete token for the password's purpose.
production.verification: Inspect the attribute for sign-in and registration contexts.

production.requirement: The component must not log, persist or transmit the entered value.
production.verification: Code review of the adapter and the example implementation.

production.requirement: ReadOnly must not be described or styled as a distinct state.
production.verification: Inspect the DOM and stylesheet for readOnly-specific treatment.

contrast.notes: The Ghost toggle is transparent, so its text sits on the page surface.
Aliases the Ghost/Hover label pair from Button.
Inactive control; WCAG 1.4.3 and 1.4.11 exclude disabled controls.

allowed: Change label, helper, error, placeholder and toggle copy; all are application-owned.
Control the field width and responsive behaviour through the surrounding layout.
Use controlled or uncontrolled visibility as appropriate.
Set the correct autoComplete token for sign-in or registration.
Supply errorMessage and the matching aria-invalid presentation from the application.
Override input.* and button.* token values at the theme layer while preserving the alias chain and revalidating contrast.
forbidden: Hardcoding colours, radii, heights, padding, gaps, font sizes or weights.
Replacing the native button with a non-focusable element.
Using an icon without a visible or programmatic text label.
Adding a strength meter, breach check, caps-lock warning or confirmation field to this component.
Adding success, warning, info or loading states.
Presenting an error on a disabled field.
Logging, persisting or transmitting the entered password.
Introducing password-input.* tokens without a token-source change and a new contract version.
themeOverrides: Consumers may remap semantic roles so input.* and button.* colours resolve to a brand palette.
Every override must preserve the component-token alias chain and be revalidated for text, boundary, focus, error and toggle contrast.
Do not add new password-input.* names in a theme; a missing role requires a token-source change and a new contract version.
Light theme is the only implemented theme. Dark mode is not available and must not be simulated by inverting values.

canonical: Render the full field: label above the control, password input and toggle in the control, helper or error below.
Use one label per field and keep it associated with the password input.
Keep the toggle visible and labelled; do not hide the reveal affordance behind hover only.
Let the application validate on blur or submit and supply errorMessage.
Pair the field with Button for form submission and a secondary cancel action.
Use helper text for password policy before an error occurs.
For registration, pass autoComplete=new-password; for sign-in, keep current-password.
Keep a stable id for each field so label, helper and error references remain valid.
forbidden: A toggle that cannot be reached or activated by keyboard.
An icon-only toggle with no accessible name.
Helper and error messages shown at the same time.
A red border without an error message.
An error presented on a disabled field.
A strength meter, breach check, caps-lock warning or confirmation field inside this component.
Revealing the password automatically without a user action or explicit controlled default.
Logging, persisting or transmitting the entered password.

invalidConfigurations.configuration: A span or div with an onClick handler used as the show/hide toggle
invalidConfigurations.why: It is not keyboard focusable or operable and has no native button semantics.
invalidConfigurations.correct: Use a native button with type=button, an accessible name and aria-pressed.

invalidConfigurations.configuration: A toggle whose only content is an eye icon with no accessible name
invalidConfigurations.why: The action is not announced and may be ambiguous.
invalidConfigurations.correct: Provide visible or programmatic text such as Show password / Hide password.

invalidConfigurations.configuration: A red border with no errorMessage
invalidConfigurations.why: Colour alone is not an accessible error signal.
invalidConfigurations.correct: Always supply errorMessage together with the error state.

invalidConfigurations.configuration: A disabled password field with aria-invalid=true and an error message
invalidConfigurations.why: Disabled wins over Error; a disabled field must not present validation state.
invalidConfigurations.correct: Withhold the error presentation while disabled and explain the unavailability separately.

invalidConfigurations.configuration: Toggling visibility trims or reformats the entered value
invalidConfigurations.why: The toggle must only change the input type; mutating the value can break the password.
invalidConfigurations.correct: Preserve the exact value across visibility changes.

invalidConfigurations.configuration: A strength meter or breach check embedded in PasswordInput
invalidConfigurations.why: No tokens, states or accessible announcement pattern exist for those capabilities.
invalidConfigurations.correct: Request a new contract before adding them; keep PasswordInput focused on entry and reveal.

invalidConfigurations.why: Password managers may offer an existing credential instead of generating a new one.
invalidConfigurations.correct: Use new-password for registration and current-password for sign-in.

visual.given: The PasswordInput is rendered on a supported light surface.
visual.when: Default, Hover, Error and Disabled are captured.
visual.then: Field fill, border, text, placeholder, label and message resolve to the stateMapping tokens; no hex or px literal covered by a token appears.
The masked and revealed states share the same geometry and tokens; only the input type and toggle copy/state change.

visual.given: Default and Error with keyboard focus.
visual.then: The input focus ring appears; the field border and message remain unchanged.

visual.given: The toggle at rest, hover, active, focus and disabled.
visual.then: Ghost button tokens drive foreground, hover background, active background, focus outline and disabled opacity.
The label is visually hidden but still occupies the accessibility tree; the layout gap collapses.

behaviour.then: The input type becomes text, aria-pressed becomes true and the toggle text becomes Hide password; activating again restores password.

behaviour.given: A short or long entered value.
behaviour.when: Visibility is toggled in either direction.
behaviour.then: The DOM value is unchanged and the field remains usable.

behaviour.given: A controlled visible prop and onVisibleChange.
behaviour.then: onVisibleChange receives the requested next state; the component does not change visibility until the parent updates the prop.
The input starts as type=text and the toggle reports aria-pressed=true.
Both controls are disabled, the toggle has tabIndex=-1 and the input type does not change.
aria-invalid=true, the error text is connected through aria-describedby and the message uses the error class.
The helper text is connected through aria-describedby.
The ref points at the native password input.

accessibility.then: The password input has a programmatic label whose text matches the visible label, including when hideLabel is true.

accessibility.given: A PasswordInput in either visibility state.
accessibility.then: It has a native button role, an accessible name and aria-pressed matching the state.

accessibility.given: A PasswordInput with helperText or errorMessage.
accessibility.then: The message is connected through aria-describedby and aria-invalid is true only when an error is present.

accessibility.when: The accessibility tree and tab order are inspected.
accessibility.then: Both controls expose the native disabled state; the toggle is removed from the tab order.
The password input exposes the native required state; the application provides a visible required indication.

accessibility.given: Keyboard focus on the input and toggle.
accessibility.then: A visible focus indicator is present and not clipped.

tokens.when: Every colour, dimension and font-weight reference is audited.
tokens.then: References are limited to input.*, button.*, font.size.xs, font.line-height.xs, space.12 and space.4.

tokens.when: The dependency list is compared with tokens/tokens.json.
tokens.then: All 36 dependencies exist, resolve to the stated values and map to the stated --sl-* CSS variables.

tokens.when: The consumed CSS variables are compared with the dependency list.
tokens.then: The two sets are equal; no used token is undeclared and no declared token is unused.
They are documented as a draft limitation and no additional primitive token is consumed.

tokens.given: All four states and the focus overlay.
tokens.when: Each fill, border, text, placeholder, label, message and ring is checked against stateMapping.
tokens.then: Every visual property resolves to the mapped token; no state uses a token from the wrong state.

regression.then: It uses a native label, password input and button toggle with the documented classes and no invented state props.
Toggle behaviour, value preservation, controlled visibility, error, helper, disabled and ref behaviour remain covered.

regression.when: Searching for value formatting, trimming or logging.
regression.then: None exists; the value is passed through unchanged.
It remains null and no node ID or variant ID is invented.

regression.given: The protected token source, validator and generated CSS.
regression.then: tokens/tokens.json, tokens/check.mjs and tokens/dist/tokens.css match the recorded baseline hashes.

limitations.limitation: The Figma reference for PasswordInput is unresolved and is recorded as null.
limitations.impact: There is no design-source evidence for variant or property mapping.
limitations.mitigation: Use the CSS and native HTML reference as canonical; add a verified Figma reference in a later change.

limitations.limitation: The component consumes four primitive tokens because no password-input.* token family exists.
limitations.impact: A theme that remaps component tokens does not fully control the toggle's font size, line height or reserved width.
limitations.mitigation: Keep the use limited to the four documented primitives; introduce a dedicated token family in a future token-source change.

limitations.limitation: There is no strength meter, breach check, caps-lock warning or confirmation field.
limitations.impact: Those capabilities cannot be expressed inside PasswordInput.
limitations.mitigation: Keep them at application level or request a new contract with tokens and accessible announcement rules.

limitations.limitation: The adapter does not own password policy, validation timing, error copy or announcements.
limitations.impact: Consumers must supply errorMessage, aria-invalid and focus management.
limitations.mitigation: Follow the accessibility requirements and the native reference markup.

limitations.limitation: readOnly is passed to the native input but has no dedicated visual treatment.
limitations.impact: A read-only password field is visually indistinguishable from an editable field.
limitations.mitigation: Do not present readOnly as a supported visual state.

limitations.limitation: The React adapter defaults autoComplete to current-password.
limitations.impact: Registration forms may receive the wrong password-manager behaviour unless the application overrides it.
limitations.mitigation: Pass new-password for registration and choose the token that matches the context.

limitations.limitation: The toggle uses text rather than an icon and exposes no icon slot.
limitations.impact: The control may take more inline space than an icon-only design.
limitations.mitigation: Use the provided labels and localise them; request an icon contract before changing the anatomy.

limitations.impact: No dark values exist for the composed input.* or button.* tokens.
limitations.mitigation: Ship light theme only. Do not invert values to simulate dark mode.

limitations.limitation: The focus overlay and disabled suppression use CSS :has(). The approved baseline is Chrome/Edge 105+, Safari 15.4+ and Firefox 121+; no fallback is bundled.
limitations.impact: In older browsers the focus ring and disabled overlay suppression may not render.
limitations.mitigation: Test the named baseline before release and record unrun browsers as UNVERIFIED.

readOrder: Read components/password-input/README.md for the human explanation and native API.
Read components/password-input/password-input.css and password-input.html for the canonical implementation.
Read react/password-input/index.tsx and react/types/index.ts for the private-alpha adapter API.
Read components/input/contract.json and components/button/contract.json for the composed token contracts.
Read tokens/tokens.json or tokens/dist/tokens.css for canonical token names and resolved values.
rules: Render the full field anatomy: label, password input, native button toggle and helper/error row.
Use only input.* and button.* component tokens plus the four documented primitives.
Preserve the entered value exactly when visibility changes.
Use a native button with an accessible name and aria-pressed for the toggle.
Derive State from disabled and errorMessage. Precedence: Disabled > Error > Hover > Default.
Always provide a programmatic label association. hideLabel must render the label visually hidden, never absent.
Let the application own password policy, validation, error copy and announcements.
Set the correct autoComplete token for sign-in or registration.
Do not add strength, breach, caps-lock, confirmation, success or loading behaviour.
Do not invent a Figma node ID; the reference is unresolved.
Do not log, persist or transmit the entered password.
uncertaintyPolicy: If a Figma reference is required, stop and report that it is unresolved; do not invent a node ID.
If a strength meter, breach check or caps-lock warning is requested, report that the capability is not in the contract.
If an icon-only toggle is requested, require an accessible name and a new anatomy decision first.
If the requested surface is inverse or dark, stop and report that it is unsupported.
If the requested treatment is success, warning, info or loading, stop and report that the state does not exist.
If the password policy or validation timing is unclear, ask rather than inventing rules.
definitionOfDone: The full field renders with label, password input, native button toggle and helper/error row.
Default, Hover, Error, Disabled, Default+Focused and Error+Focused render correctly; Disabled suppresses the ring and disables the toggle.
The toggle changes type only and preserves the exact value in both directions.
Label association, toggle name, aria-pressed, helper/error description, aria-invalid and disabled semantics are present.
The 36 dependencies resolve and match the generated CSS variables; primitive use remains limited to the four documented tokens.
The native reference markup and the private-alpha React adapter remain consistent with this contract.
The Figma reference remains null until a verified reference is available.

valid.title: Sign-in password with helper
valid.code:
<PasswordInput
  id="sign-in-password"
  label="Password"
  autoComplete="current-password"
  helperText="Use the password for this account."
/>
valid.explanation: Visible label, current-password autocomplete, helper guidance and the default masked state.

valid.title: Registration password
valid.code:
<PasswordInput
  id="new-password"
  label="Create a password"
  autoComplete="new-password"
  helperText="Use at least 12 characters."
  errorMessage={passwordError}
/>
valid.explanation: Registration uses new-password. errorMessage is application-owned and sets aria-invalid.

valid.title: Controlled visibility
valid.explanation: The parent owns visibility; the toggle reports the requested next state.

valid.title: Disabled field with an explanation
valid.code:
<PasswordInput
  id="account-password"
  label="Account password"
  helperText="Managed by your account administrator."
  disabled
/>
valid.explanation: Disabled wins over hover, focus and error. The reason is explained in helper copy.

valid.title: Visually hidden but accessible label
valid.code:
<PasswordInput
  id="pin-password"
  label="Account password"
  hideLabel
  placeholder="Enter your password"
/>
valid.explanation: hideLabel hides the visual row but keeps the label programmatically associated.

invalid.title: Non-button toggle
invalid.explanation: A span is not keyboard focusable or operable and has no native button semantics.

invalid.title: Icon-only toggle
invalid.explanation: The toggle needs an accessible name and visible or programmatic text that describes the action.

invalid.title: Error without text
invalid.explanation: A red border alone is not an accessible error signal; supply errorMessage.

invalid.title: Error on a disabled field
invalid.explanation: Disabled wins over Error. A disabled field must not present validation state.

invalid.title: Value mutation on toggle
invalid.explanation: Toggling visibility must not change the entered password.

invalid.title: Invented Figma node
invalid.explanation: The Figma reference is unresolved. Never invent a node ID or retain a placeholder.
